findings.title: Coverage compares different database snapshots
findings.description: The ledger and raw counts are separate queries on an autocommit connection. If ingest commits between them, coverage compares the old ledger with newly committed trades and incorrectly reports corruption, exiting 3. Supersession can cause the same race. Run the reads within a read-only, repeatable-read transaction and add a concurrent-ingest regression test.

findings.title: Raw counts include unrelated products
findings.description: `ledger_totals` filters by request shape, but `raw_counts` counts every instrument within the session times. When another product has stored trades in those intervals, its rows appear as mismatches against the selected product’s ledger. Scope raw counts to the product independently of ledger presence, preserving detection of unexpected rows. Add a two-product test.

findings.title: Calendar pool timeouts bypass storage-error handling
findings.description: `TradingCalendar` acquires connections through `ConnectionPool`, which can raise `PoolTimeout` when the calendar database is unavailable. Neither this handler nor `exit_code_for` handles that exception, so the advertised exit 4 and structured JSON error are lost. Translate `PoolTimeout` into `TickCalendarError` and test an unreachable calendar database for both verbs.

findings.title: Runtime validation unavailable
findings.description: Findings are source-reviewed, not test-confirmed. The available Python environment lacks `psycopg_pool`; no test suite was executed.
